title: WeAD Abstract One — Act One: The Hook

segments.narration: What if everything you touch — stone, water, light — is not made of stuff at all?
segments.visual: Hand reaching toward stone, water, and light dissolving into luminous data particles

segments.narration: For thousands of years, humanity assumed the world was built from solid, uncuttable things. Atoms meant "indivisible."
segments.visual: Ancient philosophers with solid geometric spheres merging into early atomic models

segments.narration: Solidity felt like the baseline of reality itself. Information, by contrast, was something we wrote on paper — after the physical world already existed.
segments.visual: Split scene: vast physical landscape vs scrolls and paper arriving as overlay

segments.narration: Then the twentieth century cracked that picture — not through philosophy, but through experiments.
segments.visual: 1920s laboratory cracking open classical reality with dramatic experiment light

segments.narration: Quantum mechanics showed that asking a question differently could yield a different answer from the same particle.
segments.visual: Double-slit experiment with particle shifting between wave and particle states

segments.narration: Relativity replaced absolute space and time with relationships — geometry defined by invariants, not fixed stages.
segments.visual: Warped spacetime grid bending around mass, geometric invariants glowing

segments.narration: Thermodynamics linked heat to the number of microscopic arrangements a system could take. Physics began speaking the language of outcomes, constraints, and states.
segments.visual: Heat particles showing countless microscopic arrangements forming state networks

segments.narration: WeAD Abstract One proposes the next step: information may not describe matter — matter may display information.
segments.visual: Crystal and rock emitting holographic information rather than being labeled by it

segments.narration: Physical laws behave like compiled software — consistent, mathematical, and rule-bound at every scale we've tested.
segments.visual: Physics equations compiling into clean executable code blocks at every scale

segments.narration: The universe, in this view, runs on a codebase we cannot directly access — only observe through its output. Each dimension of existence may represent a layer of that code.
segments.visual: Cosmos with transparent code layers, dimensions as stacked execution scopes

segments.narration: Imagine peeling an onion and finding not new materials — but new rule sets at every depth. Is it code all the way down?
segments.visual: Onion layers revealing geometric rule systems instead of organic tissue

segments.narration: Abstract One is the foundation of the entire WeAD theoretical series. To understand it, we begin with the physicist who gave this idea its most famous name.
segments.visual: WeAD Abstract One title with silhouette of physicist at end of infinite code tunnel
